related_questions.question: What am I supposed to do if I was exposed to someone with COVID?

related_questions.question: What to do if you live with someone that has COVID?

text_blocks.snippet: If someone you live with has COVID, the priority is to minimize spread and ensure their comfort and well-being. Isolate the sick person, if possible, and maintain good hygiene practices like handwashing and surface cleaning. Monitor their symptoms and seek medical advice if they worsen.
snippet_highlighted_words: minimize spread and ensure their comfort and well-being

list.snippet: Separate Rooms: If possible, the person with COVID should stay in a separate room, ideally with a separate bathroom, to minimize contact with others.
Ventilation: Ensure good airflow by opening windows or using a fan to circulate air.
Communicate: Use phone or video calls to check on the person and offer support while minimizing in-person contact.

list.title: Handwashing:
list.snippet: Frequent and thorough handwashing with soap and water or using hand sanitizer is crucial for everyone in the household.

list.title: Surface Cleaning:
list.snippet: Regularly clean frequently touched surfaces like doorknobs, light switches, and countertops with soap or disinfectant.

list.title: Masks:
list.snippet: When close contact is unavoidable, the person with COVID should wear a mask, and others should consider wearing one as well.
Symptoms: Monitor the person's symptoms and seek medical advice if they worsen or if new symptoms develop.
Emotional Support: Offer emotional support and check on their needs.

list.title: Consult Local Guidelines:
list.snippet: Refer to local health authority guidelines for specific recommendations and isolation periods.

list.title: Test and Isolate:
list.snippet: If you have symptoms or test positive, isolate yourself from others in the household.

list.title: Older Adults and Vulnerable Individuals:
list.snippet: Special precautions may be needed for older adults or those with underlying health conditions.

related_questions.question: How long does COVID last on bed sheets?

text_blocks.snippet: COVID-19 can survive on bed sheets and other fabrics for a few hours up to a few days. The virus is primarily transmitted through respiratory droplets, which can land on surfaces, including bedding. However, the virus has a harder time surviving on porous materials like fabrics compared to hard surfaces like glass or plastic, according to WebMD. Droplets on fabrics tend to evaporate faster. The risk of surface transmission of COVID-19 is generally low, with less than one in 10,000 cases resulting from surface contact.

text_blocks.snippet: Steps to Take After Exposure to COVID-19:

list.title: 1. Isolate Yourself:
list.snippet: Stay home and avoid contact with others for 10 days after your last exposure.

list.title: 2. Wear a Mask:
list.snippet: Wear a well-fitting mask in public settings for 10 days after exposure.

list.title: 3. Monitor for Symptoms:
list.snippet: Watch for symptoms such as fever, cough, shortness of breath, fatigue, muscle aches, headache, sore throat, congestion, nausea, vomiting, diarrhea, or loss of taste or smell.

list.title: 4. Get Tested:
list.snippet: Take a COVID-19 test 5-7 days after exposure, even if you don't have symptoms.

list.title: 5. Notify Close Contacts:
list.snippet: Inform people you've been in close contact with about your exposure so they can take precautions.

list.title: 6. Follow CDC Guidelines:
list.snippet: Adhere to all recommended public health measures, such as hand hygiene, social distancing, and vaccination.

list.title: 7. Seek Medical Attention if Needed:
list.snippet: If you develop symptoms, get tested and seek medical attention promptly.

list.title: 8. Stay Up-to-Date on Vaccination:
list.snippet: Ensure you and your eligible family members are fully vaccinated and boosted against COVID-19.
If you have a weakened immune system or live with someone who does, consult with a healthcare professional for specific guidance.
If you work in a high-risk setting, such as a healthcare facility or school, follow additional workplace protocols.
Stay informed about local regulations and updates on COVID-19 guidance.

text_blocks.snippet: Remember, taking these steps helps protect yourself and others from the spread of COVID-19.
